bihar_raw_news.content: Bank Holiday Today on Chhath Puja: Are Banks Open or Closed on November 16? Check For Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Ghaziabad, Delhi And Other States By Aishwarya Samant Last Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 07:38 IST Banks in Bihar and Jharkhand remain closed on November 16 for Chhath Puja, while branches in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and most other states remain open. Check the complete state-wise bank holiday list, digital banking services and upcoming UP bank holidays. Bank Holiday Today on Chhath Puja: Are Banks Open or Closed on November 16? Check For Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Ghaziabad, Delhi And Other States Bank Holiday Today on Chhath Puja: India is celebrating Chhath Puja today in various states with devotion. Amid this, it is Monday, and many people might have also planned to visit banks for bank-related work today after a festive week. So, check your state's holiday status before stepping out! Banks will remain closed in Bihar and Jharkhand on Monday, November 16, to celebrate Chhath Puja. Customers in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and most other parts of India can visit their bank branches as usual. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has included the festival in its regional holiday calendar for Patna and Ranchi. While physical branches remain shut in these states, customers can continue using ATMs, UPI, mobile banking and internet banking without interruption. Why Are Banks Closed In Bihar And Jharkhand Today? Banks in Bihar and Jharkhand will remain closed on November 16 in observance of Chhath Puja. It is one of eastern India's most significant festivals, celebrated all around with great devotion. Dedicated to Surya Dev (the Sun God) and Chhathi Maiya, the festival is marked by fasting, prayers and offering arghya to the setting and rising Sun. Celebrated with zeal across Bihar and Jharkhand specifically, as well as parts of Uttar Pradesh, Chhath Puja holds immense cultural and religious significance. Considering its importance, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has included the occasion in its regional bank holiday calendar for the concerned states. RBI Bank Holiday List For November Are Banks Closed In Uttar Pradesh Today? No, banks across Uttar Pradesh, including Ghaziabad, Lucknow, Kanpur, Varanasi and Gorakhpur, will remain open today, Monday, November 16, 2026. While some districts have announced local holidays for schools and government offices on Chhath Puja, bank branches are sticking to the RBI holiday calendar. So, if banking is on your Monday to-do list, you can go ahead with your plans! Uttar Pradesh Bank Holiday Schedule (November 2026) Here is the list of upcoming bank holidays in Uttar Pradesh for November 2026: November 16, 2026 (Monday): Chhath Puja – Banks Open. November 22, 2026 (Sunday): Weekly Off – Banks Closed. November 24, 2026 (Tuesday): Guru Nanak Jayanti / Kartik Purnima – Banks Closed. November 28, 2026 (Saturday): Fourth Saturday – Banks Closed. national_raw_news.title: 4-day long Chhath Puja concludes with Usha Arghya offered to rising Sun
national_raw_news.content: The 4-day long Chhath Puja concluded this morning with Usha Arghya, the morning prayer offered to the Rising Sun. On the final day today, devotees gathered early in the morning to offer prayers and water to the rising Sun. After completing the rituals, devotees broke their 36-hour fast by having the prasad. The four-day Chhath Mahaparv concluded in Jharkhand today with devotees offering Arghya to the rising Sun. The Chhath ghats across Jharkhand were filled with devotees even before the first rays of the morning Sun. In the state capital, Ranchi, Chhath devotees stood in waist-deep water at Kanke Dam, Bada Talab, Hataniya Talab and other water bodies to worship the Sun God and pray for happiness and prosperity. As the first rays of the Sun appeared in the eastern sky, the atmosphere reverberated with chants of ‘Jai Chhathi Maiya’. Similar scenes of devotion were witnessed at various Chhath ghats across the state, including the banks of the Swarnarekha River in Jamshedpur, Pampu Talab in Dhanbad and Shivganga in Deoghar, as well as in Bokaro. Devotees offered Arghya to the Sun God with milk and water and subsequently performed Paran, breaking their 36-hour-long fast without food and water. The four days of rigorous fasting and religious observances immersed the entire state in an atmosphere of devotion. The large gatherings of devotees at the ghats once again highlighted that Chhath is not merely a festival but a unique confluence of faith and nature. During the entire ritual, the administration and voluntary organisations remained vigilant at all major ghats across Jharkhand. The festival concluded peacefully in a devotional atmosphere, with elaborate security arrangements in place.

national_raw_news.title: Logo and mascot for 8th edition of Khelo India Youth Games unveiled 15 Nov 2026 | 6:18 PM 167
national_raw_news.content: Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy today unveiled the logo and mascot for the 8th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games. The Games will be held across six cities in Telangana from 11th to 22nd of next month. Addressing the gathering, Dr Mandaviya said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on connecting the youth with sports and making sports an integral part of the country’s development vision. He said various sporting events, including the Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India Beach Games, Winter Games and Tribal Games, are being organised under the Khelo India initiative to encourage greater participation of young people in sports. Speaking on the occasion, Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said events such as the Khelo India Youth Games would help advance the Prime Minister’s vision of a Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat by encouraging young people to stay away from substance abuse and other social challenges. Both Dr Mandaviya and Mr Reddy expressed their gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his guidance and support in organising the Khelo India Youth Games in Telangana. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said around eight thousand athletes and participants are expected to take part in the Games. The 8th edition will feature 29 disciplines, including 27 competitive sports and two demonstration events.

national_raw_news.title: Winter Session of Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly to begin today 3 hours ago 51
national_raw_news.content: The six-day Winter Session of Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly will begin today at Tapovan in Dharamshala. The final Winter Session of the 14th Assembly is expected to witness heated exchanges between the ruling party and the opposition on various issues. More than a dozen bills are also likely to be introduced during the session. Akashvani correspondent reports that the Assembly proceedings will begin at 2 PM. Legislators have submitted over 413 questions for the session, covering departmental functioning, government schemes, pending projects and public issues. The BJP is set to corner the government over the 1,500-rupee monthly assistance to women, unfulfilled poll promises, beneficiary selection under the Chief Minister’s Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Scheme and the pace of development works. The Congress government, meanwhile, is prepared to defend its performance and respond to the opposition. The government is also likely to introduce more than a dozen bills, including proposals to extend the validity of road permits for Shimla residents to three years, regulate overhead utility cables and curb encroachments on public pathways. Ahead of the session, the Congress and BJP Legislature Parties will hold separate strategy meetings in Dharamshala, chaired by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and Leader of Opposition Jai Ram Thakur, respectively.

national_raw_news.title: Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas celebrated across the country as tribute to Birsa Munda
national_raw_news.content: Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas was celebrated across Jharkhand today with reverence and enthusiasm, marking the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. A series of programmes were organised across the state to commemorate the occasion. These included a tribute ceremony at Khunti, the inauguration of new Eklavya Model Residential Schools in Gumla and the laying of the foundation stone for another school in Ranchi. The celebrations culminated in a grand Deepotsav this evening. In Madhya Pradesh, various programmes were organised to mark Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, commemorating the birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The state-level celebration was held at Dahis in Dhar district. Governor Mangubhai Patel and Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav attended the programme and listened to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s virtual address. On the occasion, the Governor and the Chief Minister dedicated the Dahi Micro Irrigation Lift Project, constructed at a cost of over 1,353 crore rupees, to the people. Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Dr Mohan Yadav said that the life and sacrifices of Bhagwan Birsa Munda inspire everyone to dedicate themselves to the service of the nation. Manipur joined the rest of the country in celebrating Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas today, commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The Department of Tribal Affairs and Hills, Government of Manipur, organised the celebrations along with the inauguration of the State-Level Tribal Cultural Festival at the City Convention Centre in Imphal. During the programme in Manipur, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh presented prizes to the winners of the Tribal Lens Photo Competition and the Tribal Frames Manipur 2026 Film Awards, recognising their contributions to documenting and showcasing tribal life, culture and heritage. The festival, scheduled from today until the 18th of November, will feature cultural performances highlighting the rich traditions, heritage, art and identity of Manipur’s tribal communities. The Chief Minister also visited the exhibition stalls set up as part of the celebrations and inspected the displays.

national_raw_news.title: Journalism must balance Freedom of Expression with responsibility: Ashwini Vaishnaw
national_raw_news.content: Journalism must balance Freedom of Expression with responsibility: Ashwini Vaishnaw Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Journalism must balance Freedom of Expression with responsibility: Ashwini Vaishnaw ANI | Updated: Nov 16, 2026 19:03 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 16 (ANI): Union Minister for Information & Broadcasting, Railways and Electronics & Information Technology, Ashwini Vaishnaw, addressed the National Press Day celebrations organised by the Press Council of India at Rangbhawan Auditorium, Akashvani Bhawan, New Delhi on Monday. Underlining the vital role of media in strengthening democracy, he called upon media professionals to adapt to the rapidly evolving media landscape and technological advancements. He underscored the importance of upholding responsible journalism and the media’s responsibility towards society. The event was attended by PCI Chairperson Justice (Retd.) Ranjana Prakash Desai; Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Chanchal Kumar; renowned journalist Rajat Sharma, who delivered the keynote address; and PCI Member Sudhanshu Trivedi. This year’s theme, “Journalism: Populist or Responsible”, highlighted the evolving role of journalism in an era of rapid information dissemination and growing digital influence, the release said. Addressing the gathering, Ashwini Vaishnaw highlighted the unprecedented pace of technological transformation, observing that the next five years could witness changes greater than those experienced over the previous two decades. He encouraged young journalists to embrace change and continuously upgrade their skills. Emphasising accountability of digital platforms, he raised significant questions over whether community guidelines are enough in the face of increasing misinformation, deepfakes, misleading advertisements, digital arrests and harmful content affecting children. He stressed the need to deliberate on how this changing media landscape should be governed to empower citizens and address emerging challenges. PCI Chairperson Justice (Retd.) Ranjana Prakash Desai reaffirmed the Council’s commitment to protecting press freedom and improving journalistic standards. Underlining the rapid transformation in the media landscape, she observed that technological advancements have made information accessible to millions within seconds. She observed that anyone with a phone and internet connection can now become a news disseminator, but not everyone reporting the news is trained in or bound by journalistic ethics. Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Chanchal Kumar, emphasised that journalism must strike a balance between public engagement and credibility. He observed that popularity must not take precedence over truth, nor should virality outweigh verification. Highlighting the growing influence of TRPs, clicks and digital engagement, he stressed the importance of editorial judgement, fact-checking and distinguishing news from opinion. He underlined that AI can assist journalism but cannot assume the responsibility of a journalist. PCI Member and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi called for critical examination of international indices and emphasised that integrity and the responsible dissemination of information are essential as India progresses towards a new direction of development. Daily Excelsior 04:06 AM Nov 16, 2026 IST NEW DELHI, Nov 15 : Ahead of Nepalese Prime Minister Balen Shah's forthcoming India visit, the Indian Railways has approved the introduction of a new weekly train service connecting Janakpur Dham in Nepal with Ayodhya, in a bid to foster cross-border connectivity and religious tourism between the two neighbours. According to a PIB statement, the service will establish a direct rail link between two prominent destinations associated with the Ramayana tradition. Janakpur Dham is revered as the birthplace of Sita, while Ayodhya is regarded as the birthplace of Ram. Advertisement The approximately 604km route will connect Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantt, passing through several towns and cities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. The train will make commercial stops at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations. The service will operate once a week, departing from Janakpur Dham on Saturdays and Ayodhya Cantt on Mondays, though the Railway Board has yet to announce departure timings, ticket fares or the date commercial operations will begin. The initiative is expected to make cross-border journeys more convenient for pilgrims, tourists and other passengers, while encouraging religious tourism circuits associated with the Ramayana. It will also provide additional travel options for people crossing the border for education, business and family-related purposes. According to the official statement, the initiative will further improve connectivity which is expected to benefit local economies along the route by creating opportunities for tourism operators, hotels, traders and traditional artisans. Communities in Nepal and the border regions of Bihar are also expected to gain from stronger transport links and increased passenger movement. The PIB statement described the project as another step towards strengthening the longstanding cultural, historical and social ties between India and Nepal, with railway connectivity providing a further avenue for bilateral cooperation. The announcement builds on existing cross-border railway links between the two countries. In July 2023, India and Nepal inaugurated services along the Kurtha-Bijalpura section of the Jayanagar-Bijalpura railway, restoring passenger connectivity after an interruption of nearly two decades. The 69km Jayanagar-Janakpur-Bardibas railway project, being developed with Indian government assistance at a cost of around Rs10 billion ($120 million approximately), was undertaken by Indian Railway Construction International Limited (IRCON) in three phases.
